content:
Anna: heads up — noticed weird sustained RSS growth on Dedicated during a long-chat load test with MQA-Qwen-variant. memory keeps climbing and paging starts after ~42k tokens. :thinking:
Miguel: can you paste the perf traces?
Anna: quick snippet from the trace (condensed):
```
KVCache::alloc_pages() +0.8s
KVCache::evict_hints() +0.6s
kv_fragment_compact() +2.1s
page_fault_handler() spike at 42.3k tokens
heap_live_bytes +1.2GB over 30m
```
Ray: interesting — is this the rope scaling path or the MQA-specific KV layout?
Anna: seems both. repro uses long history + rope-scaling tokens. On Llama-MQA we see reuse; on this Qwen-MQA variant it's failing to reuse ranges and ends up with many small fragments.
Miguel: any kernel selection differences when that happens? e.g., int8 eval path vs standard path?
Anna: yes — when kernel switches to the tiled-reduce kernel (triggered by seq_len > 1024 and MQA flag) we get different shard sizes. The compaction heuristic assumes contiguous runs. With MQA splits we get lots of tiny segments.
perf-bot: automated profile uploaded: https://perf.internal/graphs/1769501234/kv-mqa-frag (flame, heap timeline) :file_folder:
Ray: saw the flame. Biggest culprits: `kv_mark_used()` hot, `memcpy` scatter across many pages, and `page_fault_handler` calls. Looks like fragmentation causes page faults due to random page touches.
Anna: repro steps I used:
- model: qwen-14b-mqa-v1 (ropegap patched)
- batcher: dynamic with max_batch_tokens=4096, prefer_low_latency=true
- prompt profile: multi-turn chat with long-system prompts + streaming user replies (~50 tokens each)
- run 8 clients in parallel
Commands:
```
./run_load_test --model qwen-mqa-v1 --clients 8 --max-corpus-tokens 50000
rd profile --pid $PID --out kv-frag.gz
```
Miguel: thanks. Could be our batching heuristics — prefer_low_latency causes small, frequent batches which interact badly with MQA cache layout. If we increase batching window we might coalesce KV writes and reduce fragmentation.
Anna: tried a 50ms batching window, RSS growth slowed but didn't eliminate growth. Still saw million+ tiny extents.
Ray: two quick ideas: 1) add a compaction pass that runs when live_pages < threshold AND free_fragments > N; 2) change allocation to prefer appending to existing extents when MQA split boundaries align.
Anna: compaction pass would help but needs to be cheap and nonblocking. Current `kv_compact()` is stop-the-world and too heavy. Maybe incremental compaction per-request.
Miguel: we could track extent age and hotness, then run background scorer to pick candidates. That avoids scanning whole cache.
Anna: agreed. Also noticed rope-scaling multiplier (4x) increases the number of KV slices per token — that multiplies fragmentation.
OpsBot: CC @ray @miguel — created ticket INF-2147 with repro instructions and perf link.
Ray: one more angle — kernel selection fallback: when heavy fragmentation we should prefer the kernel that streams KV writes in large contiguous copies (the memcpy-optimized path) over the tiled path. Might trade a bit of compute for less paging.
Miguel: yes, add a heuristic: if free_fragments > 200k then force contiguous-write kernel for next N requests.
Anna: I'll prototype: incremental compaction + kernel hint. Plan: patch to runtime allocator + expose flag `kv.compact_incremental=true` and a telemetry counter `kv.fragment_count`.
Miguel: add unit that simulates MQA split layout to the allocator tests. We need deterministic regression tests that push to 100k fragments.
Anna: timeline: prototype branch today, run extended overnight smoke on Dedicated, and canary to a small fleet tomorrow. Will post the PR link here.
Ray: also add histogram metrics for extent sizes and compaction duration. We'll want alerts if average extent size < 2 pages for >10m.
Anna: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Miguel: ping when PR is up — I'll help review kernel-selection bits.
perf-bot: reminder — previous similar ticket INF-1982 for Llama-MQA had a different symptom (KV reuse breaks at seq_len ~ 65k). Might be helpful for root cause.
Anna: good catch, I'll diff traces against that ticket.
Ray: ok, move fast but be careful with canary rollout — memory regressions can escalate.
Anna: will update thread with PR + canary results.
Miguel: quick question — any idea why Llama-MQA reused more often than Qwen-MQA? different packing of key/value pairs?
Anna: hypothesis: Qwen variant uses non-uniform kv pair sizes because of attention head remapping; leads to misaligned allocations and more fragmentation. Need deeper model-specific parsing in allocator.
Ray: let's meet 10:30 to design the allocator heuristics. Short sync.
Anna: on it. Thanks everyone.
